commitResults.messageTitle: Add persistent storage for task list

commitResults.messageBody:
# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/yqr/parser/Parser.java
Configure Gradle to enforce the course Java coding standard and update tests to comply with its lambda-wrapping rule.
Introduce an FXML-based JavaFX chat interface while reusing the existing command, task, and storage logic through a response API.
Use a variable-arity UI output helper for consistently emitting one or more response lines, and add chat dialogs as a group.
Add A-Assertions

The CLI loop and GUI response path duplicated parsing, execution, and exit-state updates. Centralizing that workflow keeps both entry points consistent and lets each public method focus on its own UI concerns.
The list and find views used identical loops to format task numbers. Sharing that logic removes duplication and prevents their numbering behavior from drifting apart.
The minimum width and height were unexplained numeric literals beside the named initial dimensions. Constants make their purpose explicit and keep all window sizing values together.

Task-type codes, completion flags, and the separator define the persisted file format but appeared as repeated string literals. Named constants document that schema and keep serialization and parsing aligned.
Add A-CodeQuality

commitResults.messageTitle: Use stream to find matching tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Finding tasks is a filter operation over the existing list. Expressing it as a stream pipeline removes manual accumulation while preserving encounter order and returning an unmodifiable result.
Saving tasks transforms each task into one storage line. A map pipeline states that transformation directly and removes the temporary-list mutation from the save path.
Add A-Streams

commitResults.messageTitle: Ui: allow command input to be injected
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui creates its Scanner from System.in, which makes command-reading
behaviour difficult to test without replacing the process input.

Add a constructor that accepts both input and output dependencies. The
default constructor keeps the production behaviour while tests can now
exercise trimming and end-of-input handling in isolation.

List and find responses currently print an introduction even when no
tasks follow it. This can look like an incomplete response to the user.

Show a specific message for an empty task list and for a search with no
matches. Keep the existing numbered output when tasks are present.

commitResults.messageTitle: Ui: separate task numbers from task details
commitResults.messageBody:
Numbered task output currently joins the period and task status marker,
producing text such as `1.[T]`. This makes task lists harder to scan.

Insert a space after each number to follow conventional numbered-list
formatting. Cover the presentation in both UI and end-to-end tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command to undo the latest task change
commitResults.messageBody:
Users cannot recover from an accidental add, delete, mark, or unmark
operation without manually reconstructing the previous task state.

Record an inverse action for the latest successful task-list mutation.
The new undo command applies that action once, confirms the restoration,
and saves it. Read-only commands leave the undo opportunity intact.

User messages and yqr responses currently use similar bubbles and large
avatars, making the conversation consume more space than necessary.
Errors also look like ordinary replies.

Use compact asymmetric dialogs, responsive message widths, and a layout
that grows naturally when resized. Carry command error status to the GUI
so invalid input receives a prominent red treatment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Validate command formats and event ranges
commitResults.messageBody:
Malformed parameters produce vague errors, while event ranges can
contain impossible, equal, or descending date and time values.

Recognize command parameters as complete tokens, reject duplicates and
unsafe task text, and keep flexible whitespace. Validate chronological
order for recognized ISO dates and times while retaining free-form event
details.

Adding the same task more than once makes task numbers ambiguous and can
leave redundant records in storage. Completion status should not make an
otherwise identical task unique.

Compare tasks by their concrete type and identifying details before
adding them. Preserve tasks that share a description but differ in type,
date, or event times.

commitResults.messageTitle: Harden storage failures and corrupt data
commitResults.messageBody:
Malformed records and write failures can leave the app reporting
success even though its in-memory and persisted task lists disagree.

Validate records before loading or saving and surface useful I/O errors.
Roll back each mutating command when persistence fails. Delay success
feedback until the updated task list is safely written.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use uploaded image for Duke's avatar
commitResults.messageBody:
The text badge does not give Duke a distinctive visual identity and the
user-provided artwork should be shown consistently with each response.

Bundle the image, reuse a cached copy, and center-crop it into a compact
circular avatar. Preserve error visibility with a red border and warning
badge layered over the profile picture.

commitResults.messageTitle: Improve feedback for command and loading errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Suggest likely command names when input contains a typo, and list the
available commands when no close match exists. Highlight startup loading
failures in the GUI so corrupt or inaccessible task data is noticeable.

Add regression coverage for command suggestions and recreation of a
missing data file on the first successful save.

Replace the placeholder guide with setup steps, command formats,
examples, and expected behavior for every user-facing feature.

Document task persistence and common error handling, and include a product
screenshot using a GitHub Pages-compatible relative image path.

Make the tagged C-Undo extension available in the released app and
User Guide while preserving the newer validation and error feedback.

Use task-list snapshots so failed saves restore both task data and undo
availability. Add regression coverage for undo parsing, persistence, and
storage-failure rollback.
